title: SLA-driven circuit breaker and staged backpressure for console metrics ingest
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: spikes in customer console traffic (bulk exports, aggressive dashboards) are occasionally violating downstream SLOs for per-route P95 latency and causing downstream processors to OOM or fall into retry storms. Existing ingest admission is binary (accept/reject) and causes sharp client-side errors and noisy retries. Goal: build an SLA-driven circuit-breaker and staged backpressure system in the realtime metrics ingest pipeline that can: (1) slow or shed low-value events, (2) gracefully degrade to sampling mode, (3) signal back upstream with clear retry-after semantics, and (4) automatically recover when capacity returns. This ticket covers design, prototype implementation in the ingress proxy + stream preprocessor, and a controlled rollout to select tenants.
acceptance_criteria: SLO: per-route ingest P95 latency does not exceed baseline + 30% under 95th percentile spike load in the internal replay harness
Ingress proxy exposes backpressure headers (X-RW-Backpressure: level=sampling|throttle|reject; retry-after=<ms>) and the SDK honors them in >95% of internal test clients
Stream preprocessor implements three levels: normal, sample-mode (1%), and staged-throttle (tiered by event-type priority). Configuration is dynamic via runtime flags (console-config service).
Automated canary rollout with kill-switch that rolls back if errors or client-visible failures exceed thresholds
Observability: new dashboards for backpressure levels, shed count, sampled count, and recovery time with alerts wired to SRE on regression
technical_approach: Stage 1: Admission policy engine in ingress proxy that computes a backpressure score per-request using route SLA, tenant quota, recent downstream lag, and token-cost estimate
Stage 2: Short-lived circuit breaker actor in stream preprocessor (Kafka consumer layer) that transitions between CLOSED/DEGRADED/OPEN states using EWMA of consumer lag and error rates

Stage 3: Staged degradation: (a) mark low-value events (usage-heartbeat, debug-logs) as low-priority; (b) sample low-priority events at configurable rate; (c) apply throttling to mid-priority events with token-bucket windows; (d) reject only when prerequisites fail
State & config: store per-route policy in console-config backed by Redis for fast reads; fall back to default policy if unavailable
Recovery: exponential ramp-down for throttle levels with cooldown windows and hysteresis to avoid oscillation
Compatibility: keep event envelope stable; add optional header and event metadata fields for backpressure_reason and admission_level
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal tenants + test orgs (2 tenants), 2-day burn with traffic replay harness to validate SLOs
Beta: 10% of production tenants via feature flag gated by tenant whitelist, monitor for 48 hours
GA: ramp to all tenants with gradual increase over 7 days, automated rollback on violation
Fallback: global kill-switch in ingress and per-tenant overrides in console-config
testing: Unit tests for admission policy evaluation, priority classification, and header emission
Integration tests in staging using the replay harness with synthetic spikes (10x/100x baseline) and real event distributions
Chaos tests: consumer restart while throttle active to verify state rehydration and circuit-breaker correctness
Load test: canary + scaled run to ensure memory usage on consumer nodes stays under configured thresholds
observability_and_alerting: New metrics: ingest.admission.level{normal,sample,throttle,reject}, ingest.shed.count, ingest.sampled.count, circuit_breaker.state, consumer.lag_ewma
Dashboards: Backpressure summary (per-region, per-route, per-tenant), SLO regression heatmap
Alerts: P95 ingest latency increase >20% for 10m, shed rate >1% sustained 5m, circuit-breaker OPEN >2m
Tracing: propagate backpressure metadata through span tags for correlation
comments: 2026-02-12: Aisha Kapoor: Initial design doc uploaded to Drive (see links). Called out token-cost estimator as required to make meaningful admission decisions.
2026-02-20: Marcus Lin: Prototype for admission headers implemented in ingress-proxy branch feature/backpressure-admit. Bench results: header emission adds ~0.6ms p50 to request path under load.

2026-02-28: SRE review (Jorge Mendes): raised three concerns - Redis read amplification, breaker state blowup across many tenants, and need for pre-warming when config changes. Added action items to mitigate.
2026-03-04: Marcus Lin: Implemented local in-memory caching layer with jittered TTLs to reduce Redis pressure. Added per-tenant caps to limiter to avoid blowup.
2026-03-08: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-proxy/pull/482 (WIP) - adds admission policy and header emission

2026-03-10: Aisha Kapoor: Started staging replay tests. Early results: under 10x spike, sample-mode kept p95 within 18% of baseline; need to tune mid-priority token buckets for events with variable serial size.
